title: Daily AI & Tech News Brief
summary: Concise AI, mobile, XR, and consumer technology news summaries with source links.

items.title: Microsoft researchers detail AutoJack attack against AI browsing agents
items.summary: Microsoft researchers described AutoJack, an exploit chain that can turn an AI browsing agent into a path for host code execution. The report says a malicious web page can interact with a privileged local service on the same machine through the agent, highlighting the security risks of browser-based agent workflows.

items.title: Microsoft attributes Mastra AI supply-chain attack to North Korean hackers
items.summary: Microsoft linked a Mastra AI supply-chain attack affecting more than 140 npm packages to Sapphire Sleet, also known as BlueNoroff. The case is another reminder that AI-related developer tooling and package ecosystems remain attractive targets for state-backed groups.

items.title: EssilorLuxottica and Applied Materials partner on smart-glasses optics
items.summary: EssilorLuxottica and Applied Materials are partnering on optics for smart glasses. The collaboration points to continuing investment in display and lens technology as major consumer-tech companies work toward more practical wearable AR devices.

items.title: Apple adds App Store capabilities for developer growth and subscriptions
items.summary: Apple announced new App Store capabilities intended to give developers more flexibility in marketing apps, acquiring users, and managing subscriptions. The changes are relevant for mobile app developers and creator-tool businesses that depend on App Store distribution.

items.title: Abu Dhabi-backed MGX reportedly explores buying data-center operator DayOne
items.summary: Reuters reported that Abu Dhabi-backed AI investor MGX has explored buying Singapore-based data-center operator DayOne. The report is unconfirmed, but it reflects how AI infrastructure demand continues to drive large data-center investment and consolidation activity.

items.title: Allbirds-linked Smartbird outlines plans to become an AI infrastructure company
items.summary: Smartbird CEO Nadia Carlsten discussed the company's plan to move from the Allbirds brand into AI infrastructure, including compute-cluster deployments. The unusual pivot shows how the AI infrastructure boom is pulling in companies from outside traditional cloud and semiconductor markets.

items.title: CISA warns Fortinet customers as FortiBleed campaign targets FortiGate devices
items.summary: CISA urged Fortinet customers to secure FortiGate appliances amid malicious activity targeting tens of thousands of internet-exposed devices. The warning is important for organizations running Fortinet infrastructure because edge-device campaigns can quickly become broad access points for attackers.

items.title: AI model providers expand tools for enterprise assistants
items.summary: Major AI platform providers continue to add workflow, retrieval, and safety controls for enterprise assistants. The updates are aimed at helping teams connect models to business data while keeping deployment and governance requirements visible.

items.title: Smartphone makers emphasize on-device AI features
items.summary: Recent mobile announcements show manufacturers positioning on-device AI as a core phone feature. Camera editing, translation, summarization, and personal assistant capabilities remain the most common consumer-facing examples.

items.title: XR hardware updates focus on lighter designs and clearer displays
items.summary: Consumer XR coverage continues to highlight lighter headset and smart glasses designs. Display clarity, battery life, and app ecosystems remain key factors for broader adoption.

items.title: Consumer technology firms continue privacy-focused feature updates
items.summary: Technology companies are continuing to market privacy controls as part of mainstream product updates. Recent messaging often focuses on account security, device-level protections, and clearer data controls for users.
